A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoVTL research work. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on UK Biobank, M&Ms and DVM, including benchmark comparisons, augmentation and component ablations, missingness evaluations and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds Gaussian-corruption comparisons, tabular-only evaluations, gate-behavior analysis and a loss-weight sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The encoders, missingness augmentation, gated cross-attention, TabMoFe objective and DGL optimization remain the same. DGL moves from v1 Section 4.2 to v2 Appendix B.3; it is not removed from RoVTL. Gaussian corruption is added as an experimental comparator, not a proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use UK Biobank for CAD classification, BMI regression and LVEF regression; M&Ms for cardiac-disease classification; and DVM for car-model classification. Random, least-important and most-important attribute-availability scenarios are retained. The added analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Gaussian perturbation to the augmentation comparison in Table 2 and tabular-only TARTE to the BMI and DVM robustness comparisons in Appendix C.1/Figure 7. The comparator sets in the main benchmark table and M&Ms comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce a CAD loss-weight sweep over eight lambda values and gate-output comparisons using attention-ranked attribute subsets. The added Gaussian-corruption control uses a 0.3 augmentation rate, numerical Gaussian noise and categorical replacement. Existing dataset splits, metrics, backbone configurations and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the analysis of the method: Section 5.3/Figure 4 tests how TabMoFe changes gate responses to attribute importance, and Appendix C.2/Figure 6 tests loss-weight sensitivity. Table 2 adds a Gaussian-corruption ablation. Conversely, Table 4 removes the DGL ablation rather than relocating it; the earlier attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, or reports confidence intervals, significance tests or run-based uncertainty. Averaging over missingness levels is retained. The new lambda sweep assesses sensitivity rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: New gate-behavior findings, lambda-sweep results, TARTE robustness curves and per-attribute missingness rates substantially extend the empirical record. Table 2 adds Gaussian-corruption CAD AUCs of 71.60/78.64 and LVEF MAEs of 4.45/3.14 for frozen/trainable backbones. The DGL ablation results disappear. Shared benchmark scores, including all values in Tables 1 and 3, remain unchanged; this is additional evidence rather than improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The stated cardinality range for t-minus changes from [0, Nt] in v1 Section 4.1 to [0, Nt) in v2 Section 3.5, correcting consistency with the already stated strict-subset condition. This is a limited formal correction; the loss equations remain unchanged and neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of robustness across 0–100% tabular availability and superiority over prior methods remain. Contribution (4) more precisely distinguishes transfer to an external cardiac dataset with reduced attribute availability from architectural generalization to natural images, refining the earlier broader generalization claim.

C2.justification: v2 develops substantive explanations linking corruption to loss of factual image-table alignment and TabMoFe to informative-feature prioritization through gating. It also interprets the new sensitivity results. The new Impact Statement identifies demographic bias from UK Biobank's predominantly white population and untested MNAR mechanisms as applicability limitations, extending beyond the retained CAD label-uncertainty caveat.

D1.justification: v2 reports original missingness percentages in Tables 5 and 7, states that M&Ms has no missing attributes, and newly documents mask concatenation and zero imputation for supervised baselines. It specifies the Gaussian-corruption implementation and states that model weights, as well as code, are available. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained experimental procedures.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SCARF reference by Bahri et al. and contrasts successful unimodal feature corruption with possible multimodal misalignment. Most related-work coverage is retained. Venue and publication updates for existing references, including TGV and DGL, do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract and selected introductory, methodological and interpretive passages, folds fusion and TabMoFe into Methodology, and relocates DGL to the appendix. Author information and citation style also change. These are localized rewrites and structural refinements within the retained overall narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds gate and lambda plots, expands the appendix robustness figure with TARTE curves and adjusted axes, regroups Table 1, and adds missingness columns to Tables 5 and 7. Figure 2 receives illustrative and labeling updates. The conference template changes headers and placement, while most existing visualizations retain their design and content.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional evidence about TabMoFe's mechanism and sensitivity, strengthens comparison with tabular-only learning, and improves missingness documentation and applicability qualifications. These targeted gains outweigh the loss of the DGL ablation. The improvement is limited because the principal benchmark evidence is unchanged and statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
